tasks.title: Design PostgreSQL schema (users, tasks with user_id FK, status, created_at, indexes) and write migrations
Scaffold Express API and React app, set up env config, HTTPS-ready settings, linting and PostgreSQL connection
Build auth API: register and login with bcrypt hashing, JWT issuance and verification middleware, validation and error responses
Build Login and Register screens with validation, show/hide password, error banner, token storage and protected routes, plus Account screen with log out
Build create-task API (POST /tasks) with title validation, optional description (max 500) and per-user ownership
Build complete/reopen API (PATCH /tasks/:id) with ownership check returning 403 for cross-user access
Build delete API (DELETE /tasks/:id) with permanent removal and ownership check returning 403
Build list API (GET /tasks?status=all|active|completed) scoped to the user, newest first, with index for performance
Create design tokens and shared UI components (buttons, inputs, task card, modal, toast, segmented filter, bottom nav) with accessibility and responsive layout
Build My Tasks screen: quick-add input, task list, status filters, progress summary, empty state, checkbox toggle and delete confirmation modal wired to the API
Build New Task and Task Details screens: create form with validation and counter, edit mode, complete/reopen and delete actions with toasts
Add integration tests for auth, task CRUD, filtering and 403 privacy checks; run basic load test (100 concurrent users, under 2s) and fix issues
Deploy MVP with managed PostgreSQL, HTTPS, environment secrets and basic uptime monitoring, then run smoke tests

risks: Scope creep from design extras (progress card, task stats, edit mode, Administrator role) beyond the five required features; defer non-essential items if time is short.
JWT handling mistakes (insecure storage, missing ownership checks) could break the privacy requirement; enforce ownership middleware and test 403 cases early.
Frontend work is blocked until auth and task APIs exist; agree on API contract up front and use mocks to unblock UI.
Meeting the 2-second load time at 100 concurrent users and 99.5% uptime may be hard on low-tier hosting; add DB indexes and test under load before launch.
Single-developer bottleneck on the critical path (T2 to T3 to T5 to T10 to T11) could delay delivery; keep tasks small and cut low-priority polish first.
